title: Best Time to Buy a Generator: Black Friday, Not Storm Week
h1: Best Time to Buy a Generator

keywords: best time to buy a generator
when do generators go on sale
best time to buy a portable power station
description: Never buy a generator in the 72 hours before a storm; the best time is late fall through early spring, with Black Friday the sale worth checking.
dek: Never buy a generator in the 72 hours before a storm; the best time is late fall through early spring, with Black Friday the sale worth checking.
intro: Buy in the calm months, and use Black Friday as your checkpoint. The one time to avoid is the week a storm is on the forecast.

The best time to buy a generator is late fall through early spring, and Black Friday and Cyber Monday are the sale dates most worth checking. The worst time is the 72 hours before a forecast storm, when shelves empty and prices stop moving down. What changes the answer is the type: a portable unit can wait for a sale, a standby system needs months of lead time. This page covers both, plus how to tell a real deal from a relabeled list price.
quickAnswer: Buy in the calm months, and use Black Friday as your checkpoint.

sections.h: Best Time to Buy a Generator at a Glance

blocks.p: Buy a portable generator or power station between November and March, and check prices hardest around Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Book a standby generator install in fall or winter, well before the next storm season. Avoid buying anything in the days after a hurricane or ice storm is named on the forecast, because that is when supply is thinnest and discounts disappear.

blocks.p: The pattern is driven by demand, not by a secret calendar. Generator demand spikes with weather, so retailers have no reason to discount during hurricane season or right after a widespread outage. Once the season ends, the same stores need floor space for winter goods and holiday electronics, and generators and power stations show up in the big November promotions.

If you already know which machine you need, timing a purchase to one of these windows is easy. If you do not, size your loads first with our [guide to home generators for power outages](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/), because a discounted generator that is too small for your sump pump or well pump is no bargain at any price.

sections.h: When Do Generators Go on Sale During the Year?

blocks.p: Black Friday and Cyber Monday are the headline window. Home centers, warehouse clubs and online retailers commonly fold portable generators and inverter generators into their late-November outdoor-power promotions, and portable power station brands such as EcoFlow, Jackery, Anker and Bluetti typically run their largest sitewide sales of the year in the same week. For 2026, Black Friday falls on November 27, and many stores start early promotions the week before.

The weeks after the holidays are the quiet second window. Demand is at its lowest point of the year in January and February across most of the country, stock is full, and some retailers clear out last year's models when a refreshed version arrives. You will not always see a banner discount in this period, but you are far more likely to find the exact model you want, in stock, at its normal price or a little below it.

blocks.h3: Summer sales and the end of hurricane season

blocks.p: Mid-year sales such as Prime Day and Fourth of July promotions are mixed. Power station brands often participate heavily, because summer camping is one of their biggest markets. Fuel generators are less predictable, since July overlaps with the start of the Atlantic hurricane season and retailers are wary of discounting into rising demand.

The end of hurricane season, which officially runs to November 30, is when coastal stores often find themselves holding extra inventory they ordered for storms that never came. That surplus is part of why late fall is a good buying window in the Southeast and along the Gulf Coast in particular. In years with a busy season, the opposite happens: stock stays thin into winter.

blocks.h3: Spring is for mowers, not generators

blocks.p: Spring sales events in March through May are built around lawn mowers, trimmers and patio goods. Generators sometimes ride along in those promotions, but they are rarely the focus. Spring is still a sensible time to buy simply because it is the last calm stretch before hurricane season and summer thunderstorm outages. Think of it as the deadline rather than the deal.

sections.h: Why Is the Week Before a Storm the Worst Time to Buy?

blocks.p: Once a hurricane or major ice storm is on the forecast, generator demand in the affected region can jump overnight. Stores in the path typically sell through their floor stock within a day or two, and online orders slow down as warehouses ship to the same region. Even if a unit arrives, it may land after the power has already gone out.

Prices behave badly in that window too. Discounts vanish because nothing needs to be discounted. Third-party sellers on marketplaces sometimes raise prices sharply, which many states treat as price gouging during a declared emergency, but enforcement comes after the fact and does not help you on the day you need power. The choice in a storm week is often between an overpriced unit, the wrong-size unit, or nothing at all.
THE RULE
Buy the generator in the calm. Buy the fuel before the storm.

A generator is a long-lead purchase. Gas cans, stabilizer, a heavy-duty extension cord and a carbon monoxide alarm are the short-lead items you top up when a forecast turns. Reversing that order is how people end up in a parking lot at 6 a.m. waiting for a truck.

There is also a hidden cost of buying in a hurry: you skip the setup. A new portable generator needs oil added, a break-in run and a first start in daylight. A power station needs a full charge and a test with the actual devices you plan to run. A transfer switch or interlock kit needs an electrician. None of that is practical with a storm 48 hours out.

If you are reading this with a storm already on the radar and no backup power, buy what you can verify, not what is cheapest. Check the running watts against your must-run list, confirm the unit ships with or can take the cord you need, and never run any fuel generator in a garage, porch or near a window. A smaller power station for phones, lights and a CPAP is often easier to find and safer to use than a large gas unit bought blind.

sections.h: How Do You Tell if a Black Friday Generator Deal Is Real?

blocks.p: Start with price history, not the strike-through price. Many listings show a crossed-out list price that the product rarely sells at. Price trackers that chart Amazon and big-box prices over time let you see the 90-day range. A real deal is at or below the lowest price in that range. A deal that only beats the list price, but sits in the middle of the 90-day range, is a normal day with a banner on it.

Next, check the exact model number. Generator and power station lines often have several near-identical variants: a gas-only and a dual-fuel version, an electric-start and a recoil-start version, a CO-sensing model and an older one without it, or a power station sold with and without a solar panel. Retailers sometimes advertise the headline model and discount a cheaper variant. Match the full model number on the sale page to the maker's spec sheet.

Sale banners love the biggest number on the box, which is usually starting or peak watts. What keeps your fridge and furnace blower running is the running, or rated, watts. On a power station, the battery capacity in watt-hours decides how long it lasts, and the continuous inverter output decides what it can run. Compare deals on running watts and watt-hours, not on the peak figure in the headline.

blocks.p: Then look at the bundle. A bundle with a proper 30-amp or 50-amp generator cord, a wheel kit or a matched solar panel can be genuinely useful. A bundle padded with a cover, a funnel and a pair of gloves adds little. If you plan to connect to your house, price the cord and the [transfer switch or interlock kit](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) separately so you can see whether the bundle saves anything.

Finally, check who is selling it. Manufacturer warranties often require purchase from an authorized dealer, and a generator is a product you want warranty support on. A slightly lower price from an unknown marketplace seller can mean a gray-market unit, a returned item resold as new, or a warranty claim that goes nowhere.

sections.h: When Is the Best Time to Buy a Portable Power Station?

blocks.p: Portable power stations follow the consumer electronics calendar more than the outdoor power calendar. The major brands typically run their deepest sales around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, with a second strong window around Prime Day in July and smaller promotions around spring holidays. That makes late November the single most reliable week of the year to buy one.

Power stations also turn over quickly. Brands refresh their lines often, and when a new generation launches, the outgoing model is commonly discounted to clear stock. That can be a very good buy if the older unit already uses LiFePO4 cells, has enough continuous output for your loads, and keeps a full warranty. It is a poor buy if the older model uses a shorter-lived chemistry or lacks a pass-through UPS mode you wanted.

Size before you shop. Our [portable power station guide](/best-portable-power-station/) explains the core numbers: a 1,000Wh class unit runs a typical refrigerator for roughly 6 to 14 hours depending on the fridge, and LiFePO4 units are rated for 3,000 or more charge cycles. If a sale pushes you toward a bigger unit than you need, the extra capacity only helps if you can recharge it from the wall, a car or solar between outages.

Do not let a battery sale replace a generator plan if your outages last for days. A power station is quiet and safe indoors, which makes it ideal for medical devices, phones, lights and a router. A long outage that includes a well pump, a sump pump or a furnace blower usually still needs a fuel generator or a much larger home battery system behind it.

sections.h: When Should You Buy a Standby Generator?

blocks.p: With a standby generator, the price of the box matters less than the calendar of the installer. The unit itself is often a third to half of the total project cost, according to the quotes we break down in our [Generac generator cost guide](/generac-generator-cost/), where installed systems typically land between $10,000 and $20,000. The rest is the transfer switch, gas line work, the pad, electrical work and permits, and none of that goes on sale on Black Friday.

What you can control is lead time. A standby install usually involves a site visit, a quote, a permit application, utility or gas-supplier coordination and an inspection. Installers commonly report that the whole process takes weeks to a few months, and that queues get much longer after a major outage in their area. Starting in fall or winter puts you at the front of that queue instead of the back.

blocks.h3: Use the sale season to collect quotes

blocks.p: Late fall is a good time to get two or three written quotes. Some dealers run their own off-season promotions, such as a bundled transfer switch upgrade, an extended warranty or a service plan, but these vary by dealer and region. Compare quotes line by line rather than on the total, so a cheaper bid that skips the permit or undersizes the gas line does not look like a bargain.

Winter installs are possible in most regions, but frozen ground and snow can delay pad and trenching work in the coldest climates. If you live in the North, the sweet spot is often early fall or late winter thaw. In the Southeast and Gulf Coast, the goal is simple: have it installed, inspected and test-run before June, when the hurricane season begins.

sections.h: Should You Buy a Generator Now or Wait for a Better Deal?

blocks.p: Buy now if your area has already had outages this year, if anyone in the house relies on powered medical equipment, or if you depend on a well pump or sump pump. The cost of one long outage, in spoiled food, a flooded basement or a hotel stay, can easily outweigh any discount you might gain by waiting another season. With Black Friday a week away, now is also simply a good window.

Wait if you have not sized your loads, if you are deciding between a portable unit and a standby system, or if you are waiting on a specific model to come back in stock. Waiting a few weeks in winter costs you little. Waiting into June in a hurricane region can cost you the entire season, because that is when the calendar turns against buyers.

If a sale tempts you to switch categories, pause. An [inverter generator](/best-inverter-generator/) is quieter, more fuel-efficient and safer for electronics, but most portable inverters stop well short of the output a conventional open-frame generator delivers at a similar price. A big discount on the wrong kind of machine is still the wrong machine.

Whatever you buy and whenever you buy it, finish the job in the calm months. Add oil, run it, test it with real loads, buy the cord and transfer equipment, and put a carbon monoxide alarm on every floor of the house. A generator that sits in the box until the lights go out is the most expensive kind of deal, because it is the one most likely to fail when you need it.

mistakes: Buying a generator once a storm is named is the most common timing mistake. Stock in the affected region sells through quickly, prices stop falling, and even a successful order may arrive after the power is out. Buy in the calm months and only top up fuel and supplies when a forecast turns.

A crossed-out list price is not proof of a discount. Many products rarely sell at their list price, so a sale that only beats it may be a normal price with a banner. Check the 90-day price history on a tracker and treat anything above the recent low as an ordinary day.

Sale banners lead with starting or peak watts because the number is bigger. Your fridge, furnace blower and pumps need running watts, and a power station's runtime comes from its watt-hours. Compare every deal on running watts and battery capacity, not the headline figure on the box.

Generator and power station lines often have close cousins with different suffixes: gas-only versus dual fuel, no CO sensing versus CO shutoff, or a power station with or without a panel. Match the exact model number on the sale page to the manufacturer's spec sheet before you check out.

A generator bought on sale and left in its box is not backup power. Add oil, run the break-in, start it every few months and test it with the loads you plan to run. Buy the cord, transfer switch or interlock kit and a carbon monoxide alarm at the same time, not during the outage.
bottomLine: The best time to buy a generator is when you do not need one yet. Late fall through early spring gives you the best mix of promotions, stock and installer availability, and Black Friday on November 27 is the sale worth watching this year. Storm week is the one window to avoid at almost any price. Whatever the calendar says, a deal only counts if it is the right machine. Size your loads, compare running watts and watt-hours, match the exact model number and check the 90-day price history. Then set it up, test it and connect it safely while the weather is still calm.

faqs.q: Do generators go on sale for Black Friday?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Home centers, warehouse clubs and online retailers commonly include portable and inverter generators in their late-November outdoor-power promotions, and portable power station brands typically run their biggest sales of the year that week. Discounts vary by model and store, so check the 90-day price history before treating any banner as a real deal.

There is no single guaranteed month, but late November through February is usually the best stretch. Black Friday and Cyber Monday bring the most promotions, and January and February bring the lowest demand and fullest stock. Prices are least likely to fall from June through October, when hurricane season and summer storms keep demand high.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to buy a generator after hurricane season?
faqs.a: It is often easier, and sometimes cheaper. Hurricane season ends on November 30, and in quiet years coastal stores may hold extra stock they ordered for storms that never arrived. In busy years the reverse happens and supply stays thin. Either way, buying after the season beats buying in the middle of it.

faqs.q: When is the best time to buy a portable power station?
faqs.a: Black Friday and Cyber Monday are usually the strongest week, with Prime Day in July a close second. Power station brands refresh their lines often, so outgoing models are commonly discounted when a new generation launches. An older model is a good buy if it uses LiFePO4 cells and has the output you need.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I plan a standby generator install?
faqs.a: Plan on weeks to a few months from first quote to a working, inspected system. The process includes a site visit, a permit, gas and electrical work and an inspection, and installer queues grow sharply after a big outage. Starting in fall or winter puts you ahead of the spring and summer rush.

faqs.q: Should I buy a generator right before a storm?
faqs.a: Only if you have no other option, and then buy carefully. Stock is limited, prices are rarely discounted, and there is little time to set up or connect the unit safely. Check running watts against your must-run loads, never run it indoors or in a garage, and consider a power station for small loads.

faqs.q: Are open-box or refurbished generators a good deal?
faqs.a: They can be, if they come from the manufacturer or an authorized retailer with a real warranty. Ask whether the unit has been run, check that the full model number matches the spec sheet, and inspect for missing parts like the wheel kit or cords. Avoid refurbished units from unknown marketplace sellers with no warranty support.
